A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same T-SHIRT research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original instruction-tuning comparisons, runtime measurements, token analyses, and component and hyperparameter ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds a 14B-model evaluation, repeated-seed summaries, a token-weight ablation, and a token-score distribution plot.

M1.justification: Equations (1)–(4) and Algorithm 1 retain the same token selection, embedding perturbations, and hierarchical selection by neighborhood mean and variance. Alternative token weights are tested as ablations, without changing the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use Alpaca-GPT-4 and Magpie for instruction tuning and the same eight evaluation benchmarks. The added model size, repeated-seed study, and token analyses use retained datasets and tasks.

E2.justification: The Alpaca comparisons retain FULL, RANDOM, LONGEST, DEITA, DS2, and IFD. Magpie retains LONGEST and IFD, also used in the new 14B comparison. Table 6 revisits RANDOM; the soft-weight alternatives are component ablations.

E3.justification: v2 adds Qwen-2.5-14B evaluation using 10k Magpie samples. For this new experiment, Arena-Hard uses Gemini-2.5-Flash instead of Gemini-2.5-Flash-Preview-04-17, as disclosed in footnote 3. The existing experiments retain their stated training settings and evaluation metrics.

E4.justification: Section D.3/Table 7 adds an ablation comparing binary token exclusion with informative-to-uninformative weight ratios of 1.5:1 and 2:1. Section C.1/Figure 5 extends the existing token-informativeness analysis with a CDF. Earlier component, neighborhood-variance, token-ratio, and perturbation-count ablations remain.

E5.justification: v1 reports no repeated-run performance uncertainty. v2 Section C.3/Table 6 reports means and standard deviations across three seeds for RANDOM and T-SHIRT on Qwen-2.5-7B and Alpaca-GPT-4. This limited addition does not establish uncertainty for the other baseline comparisons or an increase from a previously specified run count.

E6.justification: Existing Tables 1–4 and ablation plots retain their results. New supplementary results include 14B overall averages of 63.79 for T-SHIRT versus 63.22 for LONGEST and 63.12 for IFD; token-weight averages of 70.91 versus 70.54 and 70.56; three-seed summaries; and additional token-distribution quantiles. These extend the evidence rather than revise same-setting headline performance.

T1.justification: The optimization setting, IFD and S-IFD definitions, token-level derivation, neighborhood estimators, and illustrative counterexamples are retained. v2 adds no theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, conclusion, and contribution summary retain the same claims about token informativeness, robust hierarchical selection, efficiency, and outperforming full-data tuning by up to 5.48 points using 5% of the data. New experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: New Section 5.1 explains the semantic-preservation and cost reasons for choosing embedding over lexical perturbations. Section 4.3 interprets binary token exclusion as providing a cleaner scoring signal. The model-scale limitation changes from 7B–8B to 7B–14B; existing security and theoretical limitations are retained and moved into the main text.

D1.justification: The v2 abstract adds a code repository link. Existing implementation and training details largely carry over from Appendix C to Appendix B, but the hardware description drops the explicit count of four A6000 GPUs. This changes disclosure without establishing a hardware change.

R1.justification: The same 53 cited works and central research positioning are retained. Hamman et al.'s tabular-LLM consistency paper receives an updated title and ICML 2025 venue and is renumbered; it is not a newly introduced work. The new discussion reuses existing sources.

P1.justification: v2 adds a Discussion section, moves limitations from Appendix B into Section 5.2, reorganizes the experimental appendices, and adds short explanations and cross-references. It also clarifies the SFT terminology and updates acknowledgments. Most existing prose and the core narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds the token CDF figure and Tables 5–7, adds a model header to Table 2, and introduces colored cross-references. Existing diagrams and ablation plots retain their visual content; the latter are renumbered from Figures 5–6 to Figures 6–7. These are localized presentation additions.

improvement.justification: The 14B evaluation, token-weight ablation, and three-seed summaries provide useful additional empirical support. The code link and expanded perturbation rationale also improve the paper. The gain remains limited: uncertainty reporting covers only RANDOM and T-SHIRT in one configuration, and the new 14B Arena-Hard evaluation uses a different judge. The small loss of hardware specificity does not outweigh these benefits.
